the quantum nature of the water proton is essential in determining the proton transfer dynamics of the protein.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the water protons at the surface of a protein are not localized, and that their delocalization can be described in terms of a coherent superposition of states with different proton configurations, as predicted by quantum mechanics.
the quantum nature of water protons plays a significant role in the dynamics of the water-protein interface.
quantum effects in the protein hydration shell are not only present, but are actually quite large and should be taken into account when modeling enzymatic reactions.
